title: Orchestrate timeboxed PRD handoff and acceptance sprints across Eng/Design/Legal
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We're seeing repeated PRD signoff delays when multiple teams review simultaneously (engineering, design, legal). This ticket creates a timeboxed, repeatable handoff and acceptance sprint pattern with clear owners, exit criteria, and artifacts to reduce review cycles and unblock delivery for console and private deployment PRDs.

Goals:
- Reduce average PRD signoff time from 10 days to <= 3 business days for non-blocking items.
- Create a lightweight cadence (48–72h sprint windows) for initial review + one follow-up cycle.
- Define required artifacts per reviewer (eng: API contract + perf targets, design: flows & accessibility notes, legal: data residency and export-control checklist).

Scope:
- Create the acceptance sprint template and checklist (Confluence).
- Pilot with the model-version-pinning PRD and the structured-output change PRD.
- Automations: add calendar templates + PRD label triggers in Linear to enforce windows.
- Exclude deeply regulatory changes which require extended legal intake (these will follow existing legal intake lanes).

Deliverables:
- Acceptance sprint playbook (Confluence link).
- Linear workflow with two new labels: "acceptance-window" and "acceptance-blocked".
- Figma review flow with annotated signoff layer.
- Short checklist that maps PRD sections to required reviewer artifacts.

Success metrics:
- Median PRD review time <= 3 business days for pilot PRDs.
- >= 80% of PRDs in pilot include all required artifacts at first handoff.
- Fewer than 1 follow-up meeting per PRD on average.

Acceptance criteria (final):
- Playbook published and linked from PRD template.
- Automation created in Linear to auto-assign reviewers and schedule the 72h review window.
- Two pilot PRDs complete the sprint and obtain formal signoff by Eng/Design/Legal using the checklist.

Owners & roles:
- PM lead (owner): Arjun Patel (assignee) — coordinates pilot, tracks metrics.
- Engineering reviewer: Lena Kowalski — verifies API contract & perf guardrails.
- Design reviewer: Diego Ruiz — verifies flows, prototypes, accessibility notes.
- Legal reviewer: Catalina Park — completes data residency & controls check.
- DX/Automation: Samir Gupta — implements Linear labels + calendar automation.

Key artifacts (links below): PRD template, Confluence playbook, Figma review file, example PRDs, GH PRs for automation DSL.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Legal workload spikes and cannot meet 72h window. Mitigation: Include a legal triage step and escalation lane; mark regulatory PRDs out of scope.
- Risk: Teams don't attach required artifacts. Mitigation: Make checklist part of PRD template and fail-fast validation in PRD creation flow.

Timeline:
- 2026-02-10: Kickoff & draft checklist.
- 2026-02-17: Automation spec and calendar template ready.
- 2026-02-24 to 2026-03-03: Pilot PRD 1 review window.
- 2026-03-04 to 2026-03-11: Pilot PRD 2 review window.
- 2026-03-12: Retrospective and decision on rollout.

Next steps (short-term):
1) PM to finalize acceptance checklist (Arjun) — due 2026-02-12.
2) Engineering to author minimal API contract template for reviewers (Lena) — due 2026-02-16.
3) Legal to confirm which PRD categories require extended intake (Catalina) — due 2026-02-15.
4) DX to implement Linear label automation (Samir) — spec by 2026-02-17.

Notes: This is intended as a lightweight, iterative playbook. If the pilot shows >20% of PRDs still blocked beyond 5 days, we'll reconvene for process rework and consider dedicated legal QA slots in calendar.
